Subject: ACME POC — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Tim / Laura — great to meet this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of ask:
- ACME wants a 4-week POC to validate Redwood's retrieval-augmented generation for internal knowledge search and summarization. Key KPIs: answer accuracy (factual recall), latency (95p <= 600ms), and token cost per query.

Proposed POC scope / timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria & access (S3 + API creds).
- Week 1-2: offline evals and model selection (we'll run your test set + 500 sampled queries).
- Week 3: online shadow & compare online vs offline metrics on a 10% shadow traffic slice.
- Week 4: wrap-up, handoff, and decision meeting.

Success criteria (draft):
1) Precision@3 >= 80% on curated test set
2) Human-rated helpfulness score >= 4/5 on a blind eval (n=100)
3) 95th pct latency <= 600ms in shadow mode
4) Token cost <= $0.008 per query (estimate)

Ownership / asks:
- ACME: share test set + access; assign one technical PM and one reviewer for human evals.
- Redwood: deliver eval plan, run offline & shadow runs, provide grading rubric and final report.

Attachments: draft eval plan (acme_eval_plan_v1.pdf) and POC scope spreadsheet (redwood_poc_scope.xlsx).

Can you confirm that the success criteria look sane and whether ACME prefers we prioritize offline evals first or go straight to a short shadow run?

Thanks — I'll loop in Rachel & Neha for rubric/measurement details.

—

Laura — perfect, appreciate the quick feedback. Short answers inline: 

1) Test set size: 1,200 is great — we'll sample 500 for initial offline runs and keep the rest for stratified checks. That will be statistically reasonable for precision estimates at the level you care about.

2) Rubric: attached below in this thread (see message from Rachel). High-level we'll do both automated metrics (Precision@K, recall on labeled answers) and a human blind rating (helpfulness, correctness, hallucination).

3) Offline-first approach: agree. We'll run offline evals first, then do a 48-hour shadow (10% traffic slice) to validate latency and user-visible behavior. If offline indicates major regressions we'll pause and iterate on prompts/model variant before shadowing.

Green/Amber/Red proposal (mapping to exec-friendly status):
- Green = all success criteria met (Precision@3 >=80%, human >=4, latency <=600ms)
- Amber = one KPI marginally below target (e.g., Precision 75-79% or median latency within 20% of SLA) — remediation plan required
- Red = more than one KPI below threshold or a single KPI significantly below (Precision <70% or human <=3) — stop and re-scope

Next steps: we'll send a formal eval plan and rubric by EOD; Rachel will propose concrete human evaluation questions and ownership.

—
Marissa

Subject: Re: ACME POC — eval rubric & measurement details

Hi team — sharing the draft rubric and process below (attached as acme_eval_plan_v1.pdf in Marissa's original email). Summary: 

Offline evals (run by Redwood on ACME test set):
- Automated metrics: Precision@1/3/5, Exact-match rate, and token-cost estimate per query.
- Sampling: random sample of 500 queries stratified by intent (search, summarize, extract).
- Acceptance: Precision@3 >= 80% = pass.

Human blind eval (ACME reviewers + Redwood annotators):
- Sample: 100 queries drawn from production-like traffic; responses presented blind (no model labels).
- Rating scale 1-5 on: Helpfulness, Correctness, Hallucination (binary yes/no).
- Pass threshold: average Helpfulness >= 4.0 AND Hallucination flagged in <= 10% of samples.
- Ownership: ACME provides 2 reviewers for the human eval; Redwood provides 2 annotators and handles aggregation.

Online shadow (48 hours, 10% traffic):
- Metrics: latency p50/p95, error rate, production-triggered fallback rate, live quality sampling (5% of responded queries flagged for manual review).
- Safety: ACME legal will review sampled responses; Redwood will mute any flagged responses and roll back if severity criteria met.

Grading & report:
- We'll produce a single scorecard mapping the automated + human metrics to Green/Amber/Red with short remediation notes.
- Timeline: Redwood to run offline evals within 5 business days of receiving test set and creds. Shadow to be scheduled in Week 3 pending offline pass.

Open questions for ACME:
- Who is the primary contact for granting S3 access / API keys?
- Does ACME want the 100 human eval samples to be proportionally weighted to internal-facing vs external-facing queries?

If you confirm these, we'll lock timelines and share the DocuSign for the POC SOW.

Thanks — Rachel
